feedback.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)<0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies below the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=-x(x+3)(x-2)(x-4)$ are $x=-3,$ $x=0,$ $x=2$ and $x=4,$ which are all simple roots.

Also, $P(x)$ is a quartic polynomial with a negative leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/889f60e9a8dac71f99dd7e676b77c3e0a1eb7b944305e21b9d4d1b6897dbbb15.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)<0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is below the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-3)⋃(0,2)⋃(4,\infty ).$
